metadataReview.note: The Belarusian Wikipedia describes the Russian and Cossack siege of the fortified town of Bykhaw, then Stary Bykhaw, beginning in 1654 and lasting into 1655; that article is the only fetched source for the siege itself. The official Bykhaw district page documents the town's bastioned fortifications and castle, built from 1611 and completed by 1637, standing as the town's fortress at the time of the war; it dates its reported wartime damage to the castle to 1659, which is not used for this siege. The atlas point is the gazetteer feature for Bykhaw Castle, a fortress reference for the besieged town. It does not locate the besiegers' lines or the full circuit of the town defences. The existing year-precision start is retained and no end date is added. Strengths, losses and equipment are not inferred.
